quizzes.title: Instrument Safari
quizzes.description: Strings, keys, drums and the building blocks of music.

questions.q: How many keys does a standard modern piano have?
questions.note: 52 of the keys are white and 36 are black.

questions.q: The sitar is a string instrument.
questions.note: Besides its playing strings, a sitar has sympathetic strings that resonate on their own.

questions.q: The trumpet belongs to which family of instruments?
questions.note: Brass players make their sound by buzzing their lips into the mouthpiece.

questions.q: How many strings does a standard acoustic guitar have?
questions.note: Standard tuning, from the lowest string, is E, A, D, G, B, E.

questions.q: How many lines make up a standard musical staff (stave)?
questions.note: Accept '5'; notes sit on the lines and in the four spaces between them.

questions.q: Which of these is a woodwind instrument?
questions.note: The clarinet uses a single reed clamped to its mouthpiece.

questions.q: In sheet music, what does the Italian marking 'forte' mean?
questions.note: The piano's full name, pianoforte, literally means 'soft-loud'.

questions.q: A standard violin has six strings.
questions.note: False: it has four strings, tuned G, D, A and E.

questions.q: Which pair of Indian hand drums was made world-famous by Ustad Zakir Hussain?
questions.note: The smaller drum is called the dayan and the larger one the bayan.

questions.q: How many basic notes are in the Indian sargam, Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha Ni?
questions.note: These seven swaras match the seven notes of the Western do-re-mi scale.

quizzes.title: Classical Crescendo
quizzes.description: Great composers of the West and maestros of Indian classical music.

questions.q: Which composer wrote the 'Moonlight Sonata'?
questions.note: The 'Moonlight' nickname came from a critic after Beethoven's death.

questions.q: Pandit Ravi Shankar was a world-famous master of which instrument?
questions.note: He taught the sitar to George Harrison of The Beatles.

questions.q: Which Austrian child prodigy composed the opera 'The Magic Flute'?
questions.note: Accept 'Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart'; he wrote it in 1791, the year he died.

questions.q: Antonio Vivaldi composed 'The Four Seasons'.
questions.note: Each of its four violin concertos depicts one season of the year.

questions.q: What are the two main traditions of Indian classical music?
questions.note: Hindustani music is rooted in North India and Carnatic music in the South.

questions.q: Ustad Bismillah Khan, a Bharat Ratna recipient, was a master of which instrument?
questions.note: He received the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honour, in 2001.

questions.q: Johann Sebastian Bach was born in Italy.
questions.note: False: Bach was born in Eisenach, Germany, in 1685.

questions.q: Which composer wrote the 'Messiah', with its famous 'Hallelujah' chorus?
questions.note: Handel wrote it in about three weeks in 1741.

questions.q: Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is a legend of which instrument?
questions.note: Accept 'bansuri', the Indian bamboo flute.

questions.q: In Indian classical music, what does the word 'tala' refer to?
questions.note: Teentaal, one of the most common talas, has 16 beats.

quizzes.title: Rock & Pop Legends
quizzes.description: The bands, voices and moments that shaped rock and pop history.

questions.q: Which English city were The Beatles from?
questions.note: They played hundreds of early shows at Liverpool's Cavern Club.

questions.q: Which singer is known as the 'King of Pop'?
questions.note: His 1982 album 'Thriller' featured 'Billie Jean' and 'Beat It'.

questions.q: Who was the lead singer of Queen?
questions.note: Mercury was born Farrokh Bulsara in Zanzibar to a Parsi family.

questions.q: Queen released 'Bohemian Rhapsody' in 1975.
questions.note: The six-minute song has no repeating chorus.

questions.q: Which band released the album 'The Dark Side of the Moon' in 1973?
questions.note: Its prism-and-rainbow cover is one of the most famous in rock.

questions.q: Elvis Presley is famously known as the 'King of' what?
questions.note: His Memphis home, Graceland, is now a museum.

questions.q: Eddie Vedder was the lead singer of Nirvana.
questions.note: False: Kurt Cobain fronted Nirvana; Vedder is best known as Pearl Jam's singer.

questions.q: Which Swedish group won the 1974 Eurovision Song Contest with 'Waterloo'?
questions.note: ABBA's name comes from the first letters of its four members' names.

questions.q: Which Jamaican reggae legend sang 'No Woman, No Cry' with the Wailers?
questions.note: Accept 'Marley'; the song first appeared on the 1974 album Natty Dread.

questions.q: Which 1969 music festival in New York state became a symbol of the counterculture era?
questions.note: Jimi Hendrix closed the festival with his take on 'The Star-Spangled Banner'.

quizzes.title: Bollywood Sur Sangam
quizzes.description: Playback legends, composers and lyricists behind classic Hindi film songs.

questions.q: Which composer won two Oscars for 'Slumdog Millionaire' (2008)?
questions.note: He won for Best Original Score and for the song 'Jai Ho'.

questions.q: R. D. Burman was the son of composer S. D. Burman.
questions.note: R. D. Burman was affectionately known as 'Pancham Da'.

questions.q: Which legendary playback singer is Lata Mangeshkar's younger sister?
questions.note: Asha Bhosle was married to composer R. D. Burman.

questions.q: Which lyricist wrote the words for both 'Jai Ho' and 'Chaiyya Chaiyya'?
questions.note: Gulzar shared the Best Original Song Oscar for 'Jai Ho' with A. R. Rahman.

questions.q: Who sang 'Mere Sapnon Ki Rani' from 'Aradhana' (1969)?
questions.note: It was filmed on Rajesh Khanna in a jeep racing beside the Darjeeling toy train.

questions.q: 'Ae Mere Watan Ke Logon' was written to honour soldiers who died in which war?
questions.note: Lata Mangeshkar's 1963 performance famously moved Prime Minister Nehru to tears.

questions.q: A. R. Rahman composed the music for 'Sholay' (1975).
questions.note: False: R. D. Burman scored Sholay, long before Rahman's 1992 debut, Roja.

questions.q: Which composer duo created the music for Raj Kapoor's 'Bobby' (1973)?
questions.note: Laxmikant–Pyarelal also scored Amar Akbar Anthony and Ek Duje Ke Liye.

questions.q: Which composer brothers created the songs of 'Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge' (1995)?
questions.note: Accept 'Jatin and Lalit' or 'Jatin–Lalit Pandit'.

questions.q: The hit song 'Kajra Re' (2005) features in which film?
questions.note: Shankar–Ehsaan–Loy composed it, and Aishwarya Rai danced with both Bachchans.
